nodes.name: Receive Inbound Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point: listens for POST calls on /wf06867-document. Use the TEST url while building, switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after publishing. Watch out: While building use the TEST url; switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after you publish.

nodes.name: Read Recent from Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Document Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Newest First

nodes.name: Trim to Digest Size

nodes.name: Summarize Content (AI)
nodes.notes: Map-reduce summarization chain — handles long content without blowing the context window. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

# Summarize documents with Google Sheets and Twilio

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers knowledge-sync work end to end across Google Sheets, Twilio and Notion.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Read Recent from Google Sheets
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. OpenRouter Chat Model
7. Post Digest to Twilio
8. Archive Digest in Google Sheets
9. Stamp Completion Time
10. Persist Run Metadata
11. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
12. Archive Row Snapshot
13. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
14. Record Sub-workflow Result
15. Fingerprint for Idempotency
16. Drop Already-Processed Items
17. Enrich with Reference Data
18. Fold In Enrichment Fields
19. Load Previous Snapshot
20. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
21. Stamp Processing Time
22. Guard Non-Empty title
23. Cap Batch Volume
24. Save Execution Metadata
25. Tag Pipeline Metadata
26. Align Field Names
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Notion)
29. Send Summary to Twilio

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing knowledge-sync work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Read Recent from Google Sheets → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → OpenRouter Chat Model → Post Digest to Twilio → Archive Digest in Google Sheets → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Processing Time → Guard Non-Empty title → Cap Batch Volume → Save Execution Metadata → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Align Field Names → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Twilio → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Twilio → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Twilio aligned by hand for knowledge sync
- Pushing knowledge-sync events into Google Sheets and Twilio the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Knowledge sync work where "Read Recent from Google Sheets" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Knowledge sync work that only reaches Google Sheets when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Twilio in step for knowledge sync, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Twilio are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this knowledge-sync build
- A failed Google Sheets or Twilio call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this knowledge-sync build
- Every knowledge-sync run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets
- The knowledge-sync AI step is isolated from Google Sheets, so models swap without touching the other 32 nodes

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Notion integration token; OpenRouter API key; Twilio SID + token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**Twilio SID + token**
Twilio Console → Account Info → Account SID + Auth Token.
_Gotcha:_ The `from` number must be one you own in Twilio. Trial accounts only send to verified numbers.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Twilio: an API key/secret pair scoped to messaging, not the account SID and auth token.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole knowledge-sync payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your knowledge sync process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
